sentences.text: The petitioner - accused No.5, who is sought to be prosecuted for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 408, 409, 420, 120(B), 201 of IPC and Sections 43(i), 66, 66(c), 66(d) of Income Tax Act and Rule 205-A of the Karnataka Registration Rules, 1965, is before this Court.

2. The case of the prosecution is that, the accused No.5, who was working as Senior Sub-Registrar and other accused, tampered the deeds after registration and issued certified copies of sale deed and encumbrance certificate.
Against the similar set of charges, a departmental enquiry was conducted against other delinquents, and in the said departmental enquiry, the said delinquents have been exonerated on merits.
3. The petitioner having retired from service on attaining the age of superannuation, the departmental enquiry was not initiated.
The accused Nos.16, 13 and 11 had approached this Court in WP No.5386/2022 challenging the very same impugned proceeding.

The coordinate Bench of this Court, by order dated 1.6.2023 relying on the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ashoo Surendranath Tewari -vs- CBI - (2020) 9 SCC 636, quashed the impugned NC:
2023:KHC:29437 proceeding as against the said accused on the ground that, if allegations in the departmental inquiry could not be proved on merit, and the person is held to be innocent, criminal prosecution on the said facts cannot be permitted to be continued on the underlying principle 'criminal trial needing higher stands of proof'.
4. The impugned proceeding having been quashed against the said accused against whom the similar charges have been made, the continuation of criminal proceeding against the accused herein will be an abuse of process of law, since the probability of conviction of the petitioner herein is remote and bleak.
Hence, the continuation of criminal proceeding against the petitioner - accused herein will be an abuse of process.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER B Madhu Kumar vs The State By Central Crime Branch on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32151328/
2 i) Criminal petition is allowed.
ii) The impugned proceeding in CC No.32355/2021 pending on the file of the learned IV Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru, insofar as it relates to the petitioner - accused No.5 is hereby quashed.
